label: early first occurrence of 2/h/l/0/y/g/w/d in the original phase
explanation: Fires almost only during the original input phase (99.7% of mass), and mostly in the first ~4 positions: rate is 17% at t=0 and falls to under 1% by t=6. It is token-selective. Input 2 is the strongest (32% rate, 38% of mass, top activations ~0.25), then h, l, 0 and y, then g, w and d, with u weaker. It fires mainly on the first occurrence of that token (in_first carries 97% of mass). The token identity and an early position set how strongly it fires. It is nearly silent at the delimiter, during the copy phase, and on other letters/digits such as b, i, r. Precision is limited (~0.45): many early first occurrences of these tokens do not fire, especially when another token from the set appeared earlier in the sequence. So there is unmodeled dependence on the prefix context.
